page.layout: Two blocks: one column of running text on the page, with marginal notes down the left margin (references such as "a Ibid.§.9.", "b Heb.9.24.", etc.). Printed page number and running head at the top. No text below the main column except a short catchword-like line at the foot right.

main_text.p: alioqui nunquam fordibus vacuas esse, sicut a declaraverat: Calvinus, inquam, huc alludens, significat solum b Christum ita ingressum esse in coelum tanquam in sanctuarium, ut compareat faciei Dei pro nobis; & ecclesiae totius, tanquam populi eminus in atrio residentis, preces ei gratas acceptasque reddere. Quod si hinc sit consequens, ut Bellarminus colligit, Sanctos a Calvino e coelo excludi, quoniam excluduntur e sanctuario coeli: consequens erit ergo, non patuisse populo aditum in templum, quia non patuit in sanctuarium c Luc.1.10. templi. Aut, si fateatur populum, etiam d Luc. 20.1. foeminas, etiam e Luc.2.37. f Luc 18.10. publicanos, in templum ascendisse, qui in atrium tamen solum sunt admissi: agnoscat igitur Sanctos hoc prerogativae Christi elogio e coelo non excludi. Ceteroqui maculam, quam Calvinus contrahit e coeli sanctuario, e secretis item coelorum contrahet h Cotr. epist. Parmen.lib. 1.cap.7. Augustinus. Is enim soli Christo eundem typum accommodans, Tunc sacerdos, inquit, solus intrabat in sancta sanctorum; populus autem stabat foris: sicut nunc Christus post resurrectionem suam intravit in secreta coelorum, ut ad dexteram Patris interpellet pro nobis; populus autem, cuius ille sacerdos est, adhuc foris gemit. Sed utut Bellarminus istic judicaturus sit de Augustino, quem i De eccl. triumph.lib.1. cap.5. alias ab hac labe vindicat: Calvino certe manifestam facit injuriam, cui pro his verbis, Christum solum ingressum in sanctuarium coeli, k Bellarm. de Rom. Pont. lib.4 cap.14. adscribit haec, solum Christum esse in coelo. Quae a Calvino inter se distingui, vel inde animadvertere & observare debuit, quod in coelum Sanctos ab illo intromitti sciebat & tradiderat ipse.

page.notes: Marginal references are printed in the left margin and are reproduced beside the paragraphs they stand against. The final line is partly unreadable at the lower edge of the scan; the words "animae" and "antiquorum" in the last line are doubtful, and "Siquis" is uncertain. The catchword at the foot right is read as "in" and may be incomplete. Several marginal references have partially faded digits. Greek is absent from this page.
